subject.title: [Bug]: startup legacy-state migration never converges when .migrated archive already exists; gateway permanently refuses to start

question: Which convergence policy should OpenClaw use for already-imported legacy sources that still exist because their .migrated archive or owner resolution collides?
rationale: The bug is real, but retiring or downgrading warnings for persisted state can hide genuine conflicts if the policy is too broad; the protected maintainer label also requires human ownership.

options.title: Repair convergence in core
options.body: Adopt a narrow verified-import rule that archives to non-colliding names or removes safe residues, then keep fail-closed startup behavior for true blockers.

options.title: Gate only true blockers
options.body: Keep legacy residue visible as doctor notices but stop treating known already-imported leftovers as readiness blockers.

options.title: Fold into broader warning policy
options.body: Track this under the broader legacy-state warning policy and delay the startup-gate fix until that design is settled.

recommendation.title: Repair convergence in core
recommendation.body: Adopt a narrow verified-import rule that archives to non-colliding names or removes safe residues, then keep fail-closed startup behavior for true blockers.

likelyOwner.reason: The item is already assigned there and the same person has adjacent state-migration history, while broader policy review can pull in steipete or vincentkoc.
